chunks: And with this chain of narration, from Al-Asam, from Abdullah ibn Bukayr, in a long hadith:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: O son of Bukayr! Verily Allah has chosen six places on earth: Al-Bait Al-Haram, Al-Haram, the graves of the prophets, the graves of the successors, the places of martyrdom [graves] of the martyrs, and the mosques in which the name of Allah is remembered.
O son of Bukayr! Do you know what is for the one who visits the grave of Abu Abdillah Al-Husayn (peace be upon him), when the ignorant neglect it?
There is no morning but that an announcer from the angels is by his grave, calling out: O seeker of good! Turn towards the chosen one of Allah, depart with honour and be secured from regret.
The people of the East and the people of the West hear it, except for the two Qalans (humankind and jinn).
And no angel from the guardians remains on earth but he turns towards him when the servant sleeps, so that he glorifies Allah by him and asks Allah for His pleasure regarding him.
And no angel in the air hears the voice but responds with glorifying Allah, the Exalted.

So the voices of the angels intensify, and the people of the lowest heaven respond to them, so the voices of the angels and the people of the lowest heaven intensify until they reach the people of the seventh heaven.
And Allah makes their voices heard by the prophets, so they send mercy and blessings upon Al-Husayn (peace be upon him) and supplicate for the one who visited him.

key_terms.أَهْلُ السَّمَاءِ الدُّنْيَا: The inhabitants of the lowest heaven
key_terms.مَقَاتِلُ الشُّهَدَاءِ: Places of martyrdom of the martyrs

ai.seo_question: What are the spiritual rewards of visiting the grave of Imam Al-Husayn (a.s.)?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Kamil al-Ziyarat*, Imam Al-Sadiq (a.s.) elucidates the cosmic significance of Karbala by identifying the grave of Imam Al-Husayn (a.s.) among six chosen sanctuaries of Allah. The narration details a celestial chain reaction where the morning call of the angels at the grave ascends through the seven heavens, culminating in the prophets’ supplications for the visitor, thereby linking earthly devotion directly to divine mercy.
